learning_objective: 🎯 Journey from the classical to the quantum world! Discover subatomic particles, understand Bohr's model, and dive deep into the mind-bending Quantum Mechanical model of the atom.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron (cathode rays). Rutherford's gold foil experiment proved that the atom is mostly empty space with a tiny, dense, positively charged Nucleus at the center.

Bohr proposed that electrons don't spiral into the nucleus; they revolve in fixed, circular paths called 'Orbits' with specific energies. Electrons only emit or absorb radiation when jumping between these specific orbits.

De Broglie suggested that matter (like electrons) has both wave and particle properties ($\lambda = h/mv$). Heisenberg proved it is impossible to simultaneously know both the exact position and exact momentum of an electron!
Because of uncertainty, we abandoned fixed orbits. Instead, we use 'Orbitals'—3D regions of space around the nucleus where the probability of finding an electron is maximum (like s, p, d, f shapes).

Four quantum numbers ($n, l, m_l, m_s$) act like an electron's precise address. Electrons fill these orbitals following three strict rules: Aufbau Principle (lowest energy first), Pauli Exclusion Principle (max 2 electrons, opposite spins), and Hund's Rule (fill singly before pairing).

fun_activity.title: 🎆 The Flame Test
fun_activity.instructions: Ever wonder why fireworks have different colors? If you sprinkle table salt (Sodium) over a gas stove flame, the flame turns bright yellow! The heat excites the electrons. When they fall back to lower energy levels, they emit specific wavelengths (colors) of light—just like Bohr predicted!

exam_tips: 📌 Writing Electronic Configurations is absolutely essential! Remember the exceptions: Chromium ($[Ar] 3d^5 4s^1$) and Copper ($[Ar] 3d^{10} 4s^1$) due to the extra stability of half-filled and fully-filled subshells.
📌 Differentiate clearly between an Orbit (a fixed 2D circular path, Bohr model) and an Orbital (a 3D probability region, Quantum model).
📌 Use the Rydberg formula to calculate wavelengths of spectral lines in the Hydrogen spectrum (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen).
quick_recap: ⭐ The photoelectric effect proved that light behaves as discrete particles (energy packets) called photons.
⭐ The Principal Quantum Number ($n$) determines the main energy shell and the overall size of the orbital.
⭐ An 's' orbital is spherical, a 'p' orbital is dumbbell-shaped, and a 'd' orbital is double-dumbbell shaped.
